ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence for foreign and domestic politically exposed persons (PEPs), heads of international organizations, and family or close associates; mandatory screening against United Nations Security Council sanctions, Canadian autonomous sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act, Criminal Code listed terrorist entities, OFAC SDN and sectoral lists for USD-denominated payments, and adverse media/regulatory enforcement databases; identification and verification of all shareholders, directors, senior officers and individuals with 25% or more direct or indirect ownership or control; risk-based ongoing transaction monitoring and FINTRAC reporting thresholds must be established before funding or issuance of shares.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: British Columbia Corporate Registry – Corporate Online (corporateonline.gov.bc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name must be expressed in English or French using the Roman alphabet. Non-Roman scripts or characters are not accepted in the statutory name. The name must contain a distinct distinctive element plus a mandatory legal element for an unlimited liability company: 'Unlimited Liability Company', 'ULC', 'Compagnie à responsabilité illimitée' or another prescribed form. Romanized transliteration of foreign words is permitted only if rendered in Latin characters and not confusingly similar to existing BC names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a BC name request is rejected, the applicant may file a new name request with reformulated name alternatives through Corporate Online. A written reconsideration request may be submitted to the Registrar of Companies within 30 days of the rejection, attaching any consent letters, trademark registrations or evidence of distinctiveness. If the Registrar maintains the refusal, the applicant may seek judicial review before the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act. A name reservation that has not expired may be renewed for an additional 56-day period by filing a renewal request and paying the applicable fee before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office address in British Columbia may satisfy the statutory registered office requirement if it is a physical street address in BC designated for service of process and statutory records access. However, for an airline in-flight catering kitchen, a virtual office is not acceptable as the operational commercial substance location; airport security, Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA), Transport Canada and airport landlord requirements mandate a physical, bonded, food-safe production and ramp-delivery facility at or adjacent to the airport.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 95 (percent; CFIA, airport authority and Transport Canada inspections are mandatory prior to first food production and are routinely unannounced during operating hours)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57, Part 2 (Incorporation), ss. 2, 4, 10-12, and Part 3, s. 51 (share classes); Business Corporations Regulation, BC Reg. 58/2003; Public Health Act, SBC 2008, c. 28, and Food Premises Regulation, BC Reg. 210/2014, for industrial licensing.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, Ministry of Finance, Government of British Columbia (via BC Corporate Online).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Articles (Form 1) and Articles; Certificate of Incorporation issued upon registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital or escrow deposit is required for a British Columbia unlimited liability company. Consideration received for unlimited-liability shares must be authorized by the Articles and must be fair to the company and its shareholders.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) that the subscription for [●] common shares in the unlimited-liability share class, tendered by the founding shareholder and paid in full, is accepted, and such shares are allotted and issued to the subscriber as fully paid; (2) that the registered office of the Company in British Columbia be, and is, established at [registered office address], effective immediately, and the President is directed to file all required notices with BC Registries; (3) that [President], [Secretary], and [Chief Financial Officer] be, and are, appointed as officers of the Company with duties as prescribed in the articles; and (4) that said officers are jointly authorized to open corporate bank accounts and execute administrative filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries Name Approval / BC Corporate Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS search through BC Corporate Online, submit a name request containing a distinct element and the designator 'ULC' or 'Unlimited Liability Company', and pay the name-search fee. Retain the reservation number and use it in the Notice of Articles.
required_dossiers: Consent to use name if a surname is part of the corporate name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for confusion or objection, revise the proposed name and refile; a reconsideration may be submitted to BC Registries with written submissions within the prescribed objection window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Notice of Articles and Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries Corporate Registry forms / incorporating counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Notice of Articles (Form 1) and draft the Articles in compliance with the Business Corporations Act. Specify the unlimited-liability share class or classes, authorized share attributes, director count, and any restrictions. Have the incorporator and founding directors sign the required consents.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as Director for each director
Registered office and records office address details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Registry pre-screening queries are resolved by resubmitting corrected forms online; if the Articles are non-compliant, amend and refile through BC Corporate Online before certificate issuance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries - BC Corporate Online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to BC Corporate Online with Sign-in BC, enter or upload the Notice of Articles and Articles data, attach scanned consents, and pay the prescribed statutory filing fee. When accepted, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation electronically; the company exists as a BC ULC on the certificate date.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as Director forms
Credit card or invoice payment information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the online filing is rejected for defective or inconsistent data, correct the deficiencies in the same electronic session and resubmit; if system delay occurs, request priority assistance from BC Registries service desk.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of Registered Office and Records Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure a physical registered office in British Columbia is designated and recorded in the Notice of Articles, and that the records office address where corporate records are maintained is identified and made available for inspection. File any later address changes through a Notice of Address Change form.
required_dossiers: Occupant consent if the registered office is not the company's own premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If BC Registries queries the address, file a corrected Notice of Address Change with a compliant physical address and confirm occupant consent before the annual report review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organization Meeting and Appointment of Directors and Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Call the first board meeting or pass a written consent resolution to allot shares, adopt the Articles, confirm the registered office, appoint directors and officers, and authorize the opening of banking accounts. Record all consents and file any Notice of Directors with BC Registries where applicable.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution (written consent or minutes)
Consent to Act as Director forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director's consent is defective, the appointment is void; the defect is cured by a new board resolution appointing a qualified person and filing a corrected notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Canada Revenue Agency and Provincial Tax Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); BC Ministry of Finance; WorkSafeBC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for a Business Number through CRA Business Registration Online; open a GST/HST account if taxable supplies are made in Canada or employees will be retained; open a payroll account if hiring staff; and register with WorkSafeBC as an employer. Use the Certificate of Incorporation and Notice of Articles for identity verification.
required_dossiers: Director/responsible person identification and residency details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA rejects or delays the registration due to a legal name mismatch, correct the name with BC Registries and resubmit the registration using a CRA RC59 correcting request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal or district licensing department (e.g., City of Richmond, City of Vancouver)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the municipal business licence application with the corporate name, registered office, proposed catering kitchen location, zoning confirmation, and proof that the premises satisfy fire and health requirements; pay the annual municipal licence fee and post the licence at the kitchen premises.
required_dossiers: Lease or ownership document for the kitchen premises
Fire inspection or kitchen suppression system certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the licence is refused for zoning, apply for a temporary use permit or zoning variance, or relocate to a conforming site and resubmit the application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Health/Industrial Food Premises Permit and Environmental Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Regional Health Authority (e.g., Vancouver Coastal Health / Fraser Health) Public Health Inspection Services; BC Ministry of Environment if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Undertake a pre-occupancy inspection of the in-flight catering kitchen and submit a HACCP-based food safety plan, kitchen floor plans, equipment specifications, waste-disposal and grease-trap design, water supply details, and ventilation/fire suppression specifications. Obtain the Food Premises Permit before meal production commences and secure municipal sewer and environmental clearances.
required_dossiers: HACCP plan and food safety manual
Grease interceptor and wastewater discharge details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If inspection or permit review identifies deficiencies, correct the noted items, request reinspection, and submit a written compliance summary to the health officer; a denied permit may be appealed through the regional health authority review process.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Public Health Inspection Services of the applicable Regional Health Authority (Vancouver Coastal Health / Fraser Health) under the Public Health Act and Food Premises Regulation; Municipal Building and Licensing Department; Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) if meals are distributed in interprovincial or international trade; Vancouver Airport Authority for bonded ramp access.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial In-Flight Catering Food Premises Permit (Public Health Act), Municipal Business Licence, and, if applicable, CFIA Safe Food for Canadians Act Licence; Airport Catering Facility Operating Permit for direct ramp delivery.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy (BCENV) / Environmental Assessment Office; municipal sewer and waste authority.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not a project requiring a full provincial environmental assessment certificate unless the facility triggers thresholds under the Environmental Assessment Act; generally classified as a registration/screening tier for a commercial catering kitchen and subject to discharge permits under the Environmental Management Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Cooking exhaust and VOC/odour emissions must meet local air quality bylaws and Canadian Ambient Air Quality Standards; wastewater and fats/oils/grease must comply with municipal sewer-use bylaw limits and may require grease interceptor pre-treatment; solid and organic waste handling must conform to the Environmental Management Act and be transported by licensed haulers; airport-side waste storage must meet CFIA biosecurity and border requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the BC Fire Code with UL 300-compliant automatic kitchen suppression system; building department structural load approval; WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety clearance covering commercial kitchen equipment and material handling; equipment gas-line and ventilation inspection; airport security pass and ramp vehicle permit for direct aircraft delivery.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) — the central bank created under the Bank of Canada Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. B-2) — operates the Lynx high-value payment system and the Real-Time Rail settlement infrastructure, but is not an exchange-control enforcement agency. Foreign-exchange regulation and administration in Canada are distributed across: (i) the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), which prudentially supervises Schedule I banks and their market-risk/FX capital standards; (ii) the Department of Finance Canada, which administers investment-review policy under the Investment Canada Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. 28 (1st Supp.)); (iii) the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC), which enforces cross-border EFT reporting and AML/ATF surveillance under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (S.C. 2000, c. 17); and (iv) the Currency Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. C-52), which establishes the Canadian dollar as lawful money. The Minister of Finance, through the Financial Administration Act, may issue emergency foreign-currency directions only in declared national emergencies; no peacetime exchange-control regime currently exists.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, BC Registry Services, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than two months after the annual anniversary of the ULC's date of incorporation or amalgamation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a prescribed C$200 late fee; failure to file for two consecutive years permits the Registrar to administratively strike the ULC off the register and dissolve the company after required notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) T2 Corporation Income Tax Return and Schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; any tax balance is due two months after fiscal year-end for non-CCPCs and three months for Canadian-controlled private corporations.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months, with a repeat-filing penalty of 10% for second offences; intentional failure may result in CRA estimated assessment and prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual verification and on-site audit trail of statutory registers and the ULC Transparency Register of Significant Individuals (no external filing required)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Maintained at the registered office; produced to the BC Registrar, CRA, or law enforcement upon lawful demand.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, no later than the date the directors approve the financial statements; changes in shareholding or significant control must be recorded within 10 business days of knowledge.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain required registers is an offence under BC corporate transparency rules; fines up to C$25,000 and possible personal liability for directors/authorized signatories.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the BC Business Corporations Act, an independent audit is mandatory for any distribution company (public issuer). A private or non-distributing ULC may dispense with an auditor only by unanimous shareholder resolution; if no such resolution is in force, an auditor must be appointed. A shareholder holding the statutory minimum voting percentage may requisition an audit. There is no revenue-based audit threshold under BC law.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (CPA Canada Handbook Part I) is required for publicly accountable enterprises; a private BC ULC may apply Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE, Part II) or IFRS on a consistent basis. Financial statements must be kept in Canada and be available to CRA on request.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually, the ULC must review its Register of Members, update all share transfer records (including transfers under share purchase agreements or aviation catering joint-venture arrangements), and verify that the Transparency Register identifies every significant individual holding at least 25% of voting shares or exercising control in any manner. The annual confirmation may be performed by officers or external counsel, documented in the minute book, and made available to authorities on demand; changes must be entered within 10 business days.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 - USD 750 per year depending on the physical British Columbia registered office, mail forwarding, and statutory agent services.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - USD 15,000 per year for a full independent audit; USD 2,500 - USD 4,500 for review/compilation services when audit is validly dispensed.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No industry-specific incentives; general SR&ED tax credit may apply for qualifying R&D activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed electronically via CRA EFILE/NETFILE

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (net of deductions and adjustments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Canadian-source taxable income; apply treaty provisions if applicable.
Compute federal tax at 15% of taxable income; then apply 10% provincial abatement.
Compute BC provincial tax at 12% of taxable income allocated to BC.
Sum of federal and provincial tax; consider foreign tax credits if applicable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of unpaid tax plus 10% per month (max 12 months), plus daily interest on arrears.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident shareholder must provide a Certificate of Residence (TRC) from their tax authority and submit Form NR301 (or equivalent) to the CRA to claim treaty-reduced withholding rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate: 25% for royalties and interest; treaty rates typically 10% for royalties and 15% for interest (e.g., under Canada-US treaty).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required if total value of transactions with non-residents exceeds CAD 1 million; Master File required if exceeds CAD 10 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Not applicable; Canada relies on General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and transfer pricing rules under Section 247 of the Income Tax Act.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of income, false deductions, or deliberate misrepresentation in T2 filing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under the Income Tax Act; fines up to 200% of tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for unpaid corporate tax under Section 227.1 if they failed to withhold or remit; civil restitution and potential travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the ULC as a conduit without real business operations, employees, or assets in Canada, solely to shift profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR reassessment, denial of treaty benefits, and penalties up to 50% of the tax benefit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for penalties if they knowingly participated in the scheme; potential criminal charges for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement AML compliance program, report suspicious transactions, or maintain records under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 2 million for corporations; criminal penalties for individuals.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally fined or imprisoned if they knowingly fail to comply; travel bans may be imposed during investigation.
